content:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have moved their children to a new school just two days into the academic year.

Hello! magazine first reported the news, saying 5-year-old Prince Archie and 3-year-old Princess Lilibet were forced to leave their previous school after security concerns were raised by their protection team.

According to reports, Harry and Meghan's private security team raised concerns that the current arrangements posed potential risks to the family, including heavy traffic near the school and a lengthy commute. Hello! also reported an incident that made it difficult for the family to travel together in their vehicles.

A spokesperson for the Sussexes told HuffPost: "The decision to relocate the children was made following discussion with their family security team about whether the current arrangements were workable."

The spokesperson added: "The parents are deeply grateful to all the teachers and staff who have lovingly cared for and dedicated themselves to their family. This decision should absolutely not be interpreted as a negative reflection on the school or the exceptional care their children have received there."

Harry has consistently raised concerns about his security arrangements in the UK since stepping back from royal duties and losing government-funded police protection.

He previously took legal action against the decision, arguing that the current arrangements left him and his family at significant risk.

Speaking to the BBC in May 2025, when the family was based in the US, Prince Harry said: "I can't see a world in which I would be able to bring my wife and children back to the UK at this point."

The Daily Telegraph reported that, since they are currently in the UK, the Royal and VIP Executive Committee (RAVEC) will conduct a new round of official risk assessments for the couple.
